motivation: Increased Sericinus density suppresses Atrophaneura survival despite no corresponding reduction in FINAL visual leaf-remaining scores; transient food shortage not measured.
source_limit: Original Figshare 23170898 has 30 cages, 690 cage-day larval rows, and 120 FINAL ordinal leaf scores (four plants in each cage); no sequential edible biomass measurements or independent food-clamp factor.
primary_question: Can maintaining an independently quantified edible Aristolochia supply through critical instars eliminate the negative effect of Sericinus on Atrophaneura, compared with natural regrowth conditions?
randomization_unit: One independent complete cage/enclosure and ALL potted host plants within it; historical plant_id column in software represents whole randomized cage, NOT each terminal plant pot.
recipient: Fixed initially allocated cohort of Atrophaneura alcinous neonates in each cage

competitor: Sericinus montela present at pre-pilot-fixed density
food_access: Feedback-supported edible biomass target via fresh Aristolochia material, with sham handling in all cells

constraints: Block by plant material source, date and independent butterfly family
Track actual accessible leaf area and leaf age over development
Observe microclimate and live butterfly contact
Obtain all permits for nonnative butterfly handling and containment
No release or translocation into open habitats

Where resources permit, provide same-age extra foliage to all arms, with randomized physical edibility/access and matched sham barrier handling to decouple the arrival of fresh leaves from their accessibility.
Treat whole multi-plant cage as randomized unit; do not multiply sample size by counting four nested potted host plants.
outcome: Number of flight-capable adult A. alcinous individuals per originally assigned native larval cohort, including zeros
secondary: Natural and clamped competitor contrasts separately
Daily live edible leaf mass/area per instar
Days spent below prospectively fixed leaf availability threshold
analysis: Report treatment absolute risks and randomization-unit clustered uncertainty, with source-block effects; sample size from a blinded pilot variance rather than the 30 published cages.
decisions: If equal-food clamp does not produce exposure contrast, test is uninformative
If negative competitor effect vanishes with food access, consistent with hidden transient competition but supplementation also changes leaf quality/handling
If suppression persists despite verified food access, independently test donor conditioning and direct physical interference
Do not call plant defensive chemistry causal without independent chemistry manipulation
No proof of botanical plant invasion, because here the invader is the butterfly
comparison_to_prior_art: 2012 ESJ poster already proposed temporal resource regeneration
2023 study tested two-species density and final food quantity but not experimentally controlled time-resolved accessible food

source_stage_demand_reference.citation: Hashimoto and Ohgushi (2023) Table 1; original PDF https://www.ecology.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~ohgushi/ja/achievements/PDF/Ohgushi271.pdf
source_stage_demand_reference.units: leaf mg dry mass consumed per individual, from early versus late instar intervals; not directly current leaf standing crop or minimum leaf area
source_stage_demand_reference.previously_audited_kyoto_stages: 23 of 24 Atrophaneura-occupied cages reached observed 3rd-5th instars; earliest observed late stage day 3 in 3, day 5 in 14, day 7 in 6; observational interval not exact molt date
source_stage_demand_reference.required: Begin accessible-leaf measurements before day 3 in new synchronized pilot, then monitor 3rd–5th instars through pupation; calibrate dry-mass-to-area and within-instar demand independently

quality_separating_control.physical_proposal: Where feasible, supply SAME donor plant age/source (not just leaf age), same leaf node and collection day of additional Aristolochia foliage into ALL cages. Natural access arms get inaccessible matched sham foliage, supported arms get edible matching foliage. Record plant age, leaf position, plant nutrient and AAI/AAII measurements. Keep barrier and microclimate effects controlled.
quality_separating_control.purpose: Keep introduction of fresh leaf volatiles, time of handling and external supplementary leaf source as similar as possible; contrast ACCESS to added edible leaves, not merely arrival of young leaves. A barrier itself can change behavior and humidity, so controlled microclimate observations and barrier sham remain mandatory.
quality_separating_control.change_to_existing_arms: Four 2x2 arms retained. Access to matched-age supplemented foliage is the food clamp factor; both levels receive comparable foliage and handling. No third posthoc arm chosen by outcomes.
quality_separating_control.limitation: Even this design cannot prove all benefits originate in mass alone: larval movement/available surface, barrier-induced geometry and tissue physiology remain candidate causal mechanisms.
quality_separating_control.critical: The published 30 cages contained four plants each; independent assignment must be per WHOLE CAGE, not each of four nested potted plants.

independent_prior_art_plant_age_quality_.citation: Jeong et al. 2023 Frontiers in Plant Science DOI 10.3389/fpls.2023.1145363, source fulltext independently verified from Europe PMC PMC10265686
independent_prior_art_plant_age_quality_.fixed_leaf_position: 5th–7th leaf from uppermost leaf, i.e. plant ontogenetic age is distinct from within-shoot leaf developmental age

feeding_trial.leaf_supply: Leaves replaced whenever more than 50 percent consumed

prior_known_butterfly_performance.interpretation: Relative growth varies with whole-plant age and sampling season even under replenished leaves; single-species previously published result. AAI concentration is correlated with plant age and is not independently randomized to prove the growth mechanism.

independent_prior_art_plant_age_quality_.caution: Differences in whole-plant age and within-shoot leaf stage are distinct dimensions. Assaying only added_leaf_age_class and accessible biomass cannot match whole-plant provenance, season and nutritional traits.

minimum_leaf_quality_control_extension: For each whole-cage arm assign fresh host foliage from balanced, separately labeled donor PLANTS across treatments; do not use 'fresh leaves' as a synonym for a common quality treatment.

Record donor host PLANT ontogenetic planting year or age class when knowable, as distinct from POSITION/developmental age of its sampled leaves; if unknown, mark unknown and block by measured provenance/source rather than fabricating age.

Prespecify donor leaf position (e.g. corresponding nodes) and date, laboratory drying/fresh-mass calibration, and independently quantify C/N or leaf nitrogen in a blinded subset of original supplied foliage.
Where permits/assays allow, quantify AAI and AAII by specified validated procedures but do not assume Korean A. contorta 37-fold chemistry range applies to Japanese A. debilis.

Balance donor PLANT/source/age, leaf position, collection time and sham manipulation between resource-access arms. If balance fails, interpret observed survival differences as bundled foliage supply/quality effects.
